what_this_is: The Workshop row for the cite-principles-from-captions folder: a script the person's AI runs on the person's own computer to build a corpus from captioned videos, pick the passages worth reading for principles, check every quote against the captions word for word, and merge the principles into one ranked registry with the evidence for each.

payload.label: Keep principles from captioned videos, each backed by a quote checked word for word (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Collect the principles that creators and teachers state or show in their videos, with the exact words and the second they say them, prove every quote is really in the captions, and rank each principle by how many independent channels back it and how well their videos did
payload.description: Works on a folder of YouTube caption files (<id>.en.json3) with their <id>.info.json. corpus: one line per captioned video with its channel, title, views, kind (short or video), the captions as timed lines, and how many times its channel's usual views the video got (the usual is the median from a views table the person gives, or from the folder itself). candidates: the best 40-second windows of each video for what the person wants principles about, scored by their topic words, advice-giving phrases, a matching title and how well the video did, per channel, plus the first 45 seconds of each channel's best videos. find and verify: the second a quote is said at, and a check that every quote in the person's rows is an exact substring of its video's captions (ignoring case, white space and curly apostrophes), telling a wrong quote from a missing caption file and a quote at the wrong second. registry: merges the person's working rows (their own groups, lane names and stage names, passed in as files) into one registry of principles ranked by evidence strength (for each independent channel the best of log2(1 + the video's times-the-usual, capped at 64), halved when the quote only demonstrates the principle), with sources linked to the second, demonstrations, and contradictions linked both ways. extract: reads every part of every video with a chat model the person names (Ollama, MLX, llama.cpp or any OpenAI-compatible server, given as {url, model}), asking for the rows their own asks file describes, from any domain; each row's quote is put back onto the exact caption words and the seconds they start and end, rows whose quote is not in the captions are set aside with the reason, and a stopped run continues from the next unfinished video. coverage: videos, shorts and words per platform and channel, and how many videos the person's rows already cite. index: a Markdown page of the registry with its counts, strongest principles and their sources, demonstration-only principles, contradiction pairs, and principles per stage, channel and lane, written into the person's own Markdown template: their words stay as written, marked sections are filled from the registry, and principle ids, counts and evidence named in their words are filled in. Word-timed transcripts from other sites are read too. What the principles are about, how advice sounds, what rows a model is asked for, and how rows group and are named for stages come only from the person's files; the tool holds none. Only extract sends words anywhere, to the model the person names; with a local model nothing leaves the computer and no key is needed.

input.description: The folder of caption files (<id>.en.json3) and <id>.info.json on the person's computer, put where {input} is in the command.

output.description: The folder to write corpus.jsonl into, put where {output} is in the command.

settings_record.description: The person's list:settings row(s) for this tool as records:read gives them ({id, type, value} with id record:setting:cite-principles-from-captions~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>), or a JSON file of them: settings {terms, caps, lanes, merge, index-template}, read through tools/settings. Passed as --settings-record to candidates, registry and index.

output_schema.description: The last line each step prints: {"result": ...}. corpus: {videos, without_captions, corpus}. candidates: {channels: [{channel, videos, passages}], folder}. find: {video, second, found}. verify: {rows, quotes, bad, missing} (exit 1 when bad or missing). registry: {principles, quotes, demonstrations, registry}. index: {principles, lines, index}.

needs: caption files and info files the person already has (for example saved with yt-dlp --write-subs --write-info-json --skip-download)
for extract only: a chat model, for example Ollama on the same computer with a model pulled
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion, and installs nothing beyond Python 3. If you can run commands where they are: run `run` with their captions folder in place of {input} and a folder for {output} (add `--views-table FILE.tsv`, columns channel, kind and views, when they have one). Then ask them what the principles should be about, write a terms file {"topic": "word|word", "title": "word|word", "advice": ["phrase", ...]} from their answer, and run `candidates --corpus {output}/corpus.jsonl --terms TERMS --out {output}/candidates`. Read the passages and write their principles as working rows, one JSON per line: id, principle, kind (stated, demonstrated or stated+demonstrated), lanes, sources [{video, t, quote}] with the exact words, demonstrated_in [{video, t, how}], test, do_it, transfer. Run `verify --corpus {output}/corpus.jsonl --rows 'ROWS/*.jsonl'` and fix every BAD, TOFF or MISSING line before going on (`find` gives a quote's second). Then run `registry --corpus ... --rows ... --out principles.jsonl`, with `--merge FILE` ({"groups": [{"ids": [...], "text": ...}], "contradictions": [[id, id, how]]}) and `--lanes FILE` ({"stages": {stage: [lanes]}, "lane_names": {lane: lane}}) when they group or name stages. Tell the person how many principles there are, the strongest by evidence, and any that only one channel backs. When they want everything in the videos read, not only the passages, ask what rows they want (kinds, fields), write an asks file {system, user: "{parts}", part_header, reply_schema, rows_key, part_field, quote_field} and a model file {url, model} for a chat model on their computer, run `coverage --corpus {output}/corpus.jsonl` to show the size per channel, then `extract --corpus {output}/corpus.jsonl --asks ASKS --model MODEL --out ROWS --max-load N` channel by channel, and read some rows against their quotes before going on. When the person keeps these settings as a row of their list:settings (record:setting:cite-principles-from-captions~account~main, or one per film or piece), read it with records:read, save what it returns as a JSON file and pass `--settings-record FILE` (with `--scope film:ID account:main` to prefer a film's row) to candidates, registry and index instead of the terms, caps, lanes, merge and template files; its settings object holds any of terms, caps, lanes, merge and index-template, and a file flag beside it wins for that one setting. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: Written for mining many creators' videos for the principles they state and show, with every quote proved against the captions
